chain.label: FAA approved A320 ditching certification without validating attainability of ditching parameters power-off
chain.trigger: the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) approval of ditching certification without determining whether pilots could attain the ditching parameters without engine thrust

chain.label: No industry training or guidance on power-off ditching technique or low-altitude dual-engine failure
chain.trigger: the lack of industry flight crew training and guidance on ditching techniques

chain.label: Engine Dual Failure checklist written only for high-altitude failure; long and largely inapplicable
chain.trigger: Airbus designed the Engine Dual Failure checklist for the occurrence of a dual-engine failure above 20,000 feet

chain.label: Event occurred 2 minutes after takeoff at 2,818 feet agl, leaving minimal altitude and time
chain.trigger: the bird encounter occurred when the airplane was at an altitude of 2,818 feet above ground level (agl) and a distance of about 4.5 miles north-northwest of the approach end of runway 22 at LGA

chain.label: Flock of migratory Canada geese struck; at least two ~8-pound birds ingested by each engine
chain.trigger: the captain stated, "birds." One second later, the CVR recorded the sound of thumps and thuds followed by a shuddering sound

chain.label: Almost total loss of thrust in both engines after core damage from ingested birds and fractured IGVs
chain.trigger: mayday mayday mayday...this is...Cactus fifteen thirty nine hit birds, we've lost thrust in both engines

caused_by.evidence: two LPC IGVs in each engine had fractured because of the bird ingestion and were subsequently ingested into the engine cores, where they initiated secondary damage to the LPC and HPC

chain.label: Captain task saturated: high workload, stress, narrowed attention during compressed emergency
chain.trigger: the captain's resulting difficulty maintaining his intended airspeed on final approach due to the task saturation resulting from the emergency situation

caused_by.evidence: During emergency situations, such as the accident event, pilots experience high levels of stress resulting from high workload, time pressure, and noise
they were not able to start parts 2 and 3 of the checklist because of the airplane's low altitude and the limited time available
the first officer spent about 30 to 40 seconds attempting to relight the engines (as indicated in part 1 of the checklist) because he did not know the extent of the engine damage

chain.label: Crew unaware of low-speed state; aural low-energy warning suppressed and airspeed tape not monitored
chain.trigger: in this accident, the low-speed warning was inhibited by the GPWS warnings, so that the flight crew was not made aware of the low-speed state

caused_by.evidence: the flight crewmembers were overloaded with other visual cues (for example, engine parameters and outside visual references, such as buildings and bridges), which might have affected their ability to continuously monitor the airspeed tape
GPWS alerts were triggered repeatedly during the descent, and no low-energy level alert was generated

chain.label: Captain unable to hold intended airspeed; flew at or below V_LS on final, producing high AOA
chain.trigger: FDR data indicated that the airplane was below green dot speed and at V_LS or slightly less for most of the descent, and about 15 to 19 knots below V_LS during the last 200 feet

caused_by.evidence: the captain's difficulty maintaining his intended airspeed during the final approach resulted, in part, from high workload, stress, and task saturation
in emergency situations, when visual resources are overloaded, pilots may inadvertently overlook the airspeed tape

US Airways and Airbus manuals contain very little guidance to pilots on flying techniques to use during a ditching to achieve recommended airplane attitude and airspeed at touchdown, with and without engine power

chain.label: Alpha-protection mode attenuated the captain's full-aft nose-up sidestick inputs, limiting the flare
chain.trigger: the flight control system attenuated the effect of the pilot's airplane nose-up (ANU) sidestick inputs below 100 feet radio altitude

caused_by.evidence: The airplane's airspeed in the last 150 feet of the descent was low enough to activate the alpha-protection mode of the airplane's fly-by-wire envelope protection features

chain.label: Touchdown at 12.5 fps produced aft-fuselage water pressures roughly double certification values
chain.trigger: the airplane's descent rate at the time it impacted the water was 12.5 fps, more than three times the descent rate of 3.5 fps assumed during ditching certification

caused_by.evidence: limiting the ANU response of the airplane even though about 3.5 degrees of margin existed between the airplane's AOA at touchdown and the maximum AOA

the captain's difficulty maintaining his intended airspeed during the final approach resulted in high AOAs, which contributed to the difficulties in flaring the airplane, the high descent rate at touchdown, and the fuselage damage

chain.label: Aft fuselage collapsed and skin cracked, flooding the aft cabin and rendering the aft slide/rafts unusable
chain.trigger: These external pressures were sufficient to cause the large-scale collapse and failure of the aft fuselage frames, cargo floor, and passenger floor struts and to initiate cracking of the lower fuselage skin, allowing water to enter the airplane

caused_by.evidence: the airframe damage was caused by the high-energy impact at the aft fuselage and the ensuing forward motion of the airplane through the water

Contributing to the fuselage damage and resulting unavailability of the aft slide/rafts were (1) the FAA's approval of ditching certification without determining whether pilots could attain the ditching parameters without engine thrust

chain.label: Airplane ditched on the Hudson River about 8.5 miles from LaGuardia
chain.trigger: was subsequently ditched on the Hudson River about 8.5 miles from LaGuardia Airport (LGA), New York City, New York

caused_by.evidence: the ingestion of large birds into each engine, which resulted in an almost total loss of thrust in both engines and the subsequent ditching on the Hudson River
the captain's decision to ditch on the Hudson River rather than attempting to land at an airport provided the highest probability that the accident would be survivable
the airplane touched down on the Hudson River at an airspeed of 125 KCAS with a pitch angle of 9.5 degrees

chain.label: One flight attendant and four passengers seriously injured; no fatalities
chain.trigger: One flight attendant and four passengers received serious injuries, and the airplane was substantially damaged

caused_by.evidence: Of the four passengers who sustained serious injuries, three received their injuries during impact
flight attendant B was injured by the FR65 vertical beam after it punctured the cabin floor during impact
